summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn opens one more input path on the proposal side: question @malformed_confchange_proposal with a sourced Behaviour entry and an experiment. Source trace: stepLeader unmarshals a proposal's conf-change payload and panics on a decode error (raft.go:1305-1313), while stepFollower relays a proposal by only rewriting m.To and sending it - it neither decodes the entries nor attaches a term (raft.go:1714-1724 with raft.go:536-541) - so an undecodable conf-change payload aborts whichever node decodes it and the relay hop neither rejects nor detects it. Three probes on freshly elected three-voter clusters, with panics recovered only in the harness: the malformed payload stepped directly into the leader, the same payload stepped into follower 2 and its forwarded message stepped into the leader, and a well-formed conf change of the same entry type as the control. Three comparisons encode the duties that a proposal the node cannot decode must be rejected rather than aborting it, and that relaying must not let the abort land on the leader (both expected violated), with the valid change (expected holds). Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, the shape the experiment is built to measure: direct and forwarded malformed proposals both abort the leader with the verbatim decode error 'unexpected EOF' and leave the index unchanged, the forwarding follower neither panics nor refuses (one message to node 1), and the valid control is appended without aborting (index 1 to 2). Limitations state that the payload is a harness-constructed undecodable byte sequence, that the transport and admission layer are outside the captured package, that only the EntryConfChangeV2 variant was executed, and that reachability through a real peer is a question for human review; the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
